messages.subject: New entropy values after major changes in tidy LPA
messages.subject_clean: New entropy values after major changes in tidy LPA
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
thank you so much for the update to 1.0.0! I think it is way easiert to get an overview over different models and number of profiles now!

I ran a profile analysis after the update again and encountered two problems and was hoping that you could help me with them.
1) It seems like values for entropy changed dramatically? So I was wandering whether you changed something in how entropy is estimated?
2) I now receive error messages which did not occur before: value out of range in 'gammafn'. What does this mean and is there a reason why it did not appear in the earlier versions of tidy LPA?

Thank you so much in advance!

messages.subject: Error with estimate_profiles when model !=1
messages.body_plain:
I'm using tidyLPA 1.0.0 with mclust. I use it to get some values I can't get directly from mclust, like AIC or Tolerance).
I'm having a problem and I wonder if you could help me.

My model is VVE and my df is called lpa.
If I run

> lpa %>%
+            estimate_profiles(n_profiles=models.to.test)
tidyLPA analysis using mclust:

 Model Classes AIC       BIC       Entropy prob_min prob_max n_min n_max BLRT_p
 1     2       25441.423 25547.015 0.807   0.022    0.160    0.312 0.688 0.010
 1     3       24681.423 24825.918 0.800   0.075    0.890    0.089 0.489 0.010
 1     4       24424.577 24607.973 0.777   0.000    0.029    0.027 0.406 0.010
 1     5       24274.329 24496.628 0.787   0.000    0.016    0.028 0.407 0.010
 1     6       24248.393 24509.595 0.682   0.000    0.065    0.027 0.314 0.010
 1     7       24212.576 24512.680 0.650   0.082    0.140    0.026 0.312 0.010
Warning message:

One or more analyses resulted in warnings! Examine these analyses carefully: model_1_class_4, model_1_class_5, model_1_class_6

it works fine.

But if I add the argument models=6 or
variances = "varying", covariances = "varying"

I get an error:

> lpa %>%
+            estimate_profiles(n_profiles=models.to.test, models=6)
The 'variances'/'covariances' arguments were ignored in favor of the 'models' argument.
Error in MclustBootstrap(out$model, nboot = 100, type = "bs", verbose = FALSE) :
  object must be of class 'Mclust' or 'densityMclust'

I get the same error if I run the code from the example in the documentation for estimate_profiles {tidyLPA}

> # Example 3:
> iris_sample %>%
+     subset(select = c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width",
+                       "Petal.Length")) %>%
+     estimate_profiles(n_profiles = 1:4, variances = c("equal", "varying"),
+                       covariances = c("zero", "zero"))
Error in MclustBootstrap(out$model, nboot = 100, type = "bs", verbose = FALSE) :
  object must be of class 'Mclust' or 'densityMclust'

Do you have an idea of which the problem is? Or if I can get AIC and Tolerance directly from mclust?

Ricardo Gouveia Rodrigues
Universidade da Beira Interior
Covilhã
Portugal

messages.subject: tidyLPA
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

My name is Pita.
I am trying to create Latent Profiles from three variables using tidyLPA package in R I followed the instructions on https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/tidyLPA/vignettes/Introduction_to_tidyLPA.html

Here is the code line I used, the intention is to create 5 latent profiles.

SUBGROUP<-cbind(CLASTA$PERSONAL, CLASTA$NEUTRAL, CLASTA$MARKETER)
MCLUST_PROFILES<-SUBGROUP[,1:3]%>%
  select(PERSONAL, NEUTRAL, MARKETER)%>%
  single_imputation()%>% estimate_profiles(5)

However, I kept on getting an error message

> MCLUST_PROFILES<-SUBGROUP[,1:3]%>%
+   select(PERSONAL, NEUTRAL, MARKETER)%>%
+   single_imputation()%>% estimate_profiles(5)
Error in UseMethod("select_") :
  no applicable method for 'select_' applied to an object of class "c('matrix', 'double', 'numeric')"

I would be very appreciative if you could offer a piece of advice on this as well as a code line for MplusAutomation since I have it installed on my computer. I would also like to compare three solutions 3, 4, and 5 latent profiles.

Thank you so much for your time.
--------------
Peter J. MKUMBO, Ph.D.
Department of Parks, Recreation & Tourism Management
Clemson University
270 Lehotsky Hall
Clemson, SC, 29634-0735
pmk...@g.clemson.edu

Hi am currently working on my first LPA.

To do further analyses I would like to export the data frame with the profile inidcators and a person code which was in the original data frame.
I used the following syntax:

M1_3 <- d %>%
  select(ZM_SArt_2_sum, ZEE_M, ZCE_M)%>%
  estimate_profiles(n_profiles=3,models = 1)%>%
  get_data(M1_3)

However although d has 1661 variables and only three are used for the profiles the M1_3 dataframe has only 9 variables all of them concerning the estimated model but none of the original data besides my three indicator variables.

How can I return a data frame with the model information as profile and probability, and variables of the original data frame?

Thank you so much!

messages.subject: Re: New entropy values after major changes in tidy LPA
messages.subject_clean: New entropy values after major changes in tidy LPA
messages.body_plain:
Hi, thank you for your message. In short: there was an error in how the entropy statistic was calculated previously (when using {mclust}). Previously, it was calculated simply as the mean of the posterior probability that was highest (of all of the classes) for each case.

I think Caspar (copied here) may be able to weigh in on how it's calculated now. I'm responsible for the incorrect calculation and Caspar is responsible for correcting it!

I'm sorry for this issue, it was something we were very concerned about after noticing it and is something that motivated the new version.
Josh

--

messages.subject: NA/NaN error
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

I am using tidyLPA to produce mclust profile estimations for a dataset of continuous values between 0 and 100, and keep producing the NA/NaN error below:

> imp.all %>%
+   select(tbank, tco, trel, tedu, tgov, tlab, tpress, tmed, tcourt, tsci, tcongr, tmil) %>%
+   single_imputation() %>%
+   estimate_profiles(1:4,
+                     variances = c("equal", "varying"),
+                     covariances = c("zero", "varying")) %>%
+   compare_solutions(statistics = c("AIC", "BIC"))
Error in mdpwst[i]:mdpwfin[i] : NA/NaN argument

I've checked that there are no NAs in the columns i've selected. I imagine it is a simple error I've made, but I can't quite figure out, looking at the source code, what is producing this error and how to prevent it. Any guidance you can provide would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks so much,
Charlotte

messages.subject: Re: How to return original data frame
messages.subject_clean: How to return original data frame
messages.body_plain:
Hi, and thanks for your question!

If you want to add these to the original data.frame, you could run:

M1_3 <- d %>%
  select(ZM_SArt_2_sum, ZEE_M, ZCE_M)%>%
  estimate_profiles(n_profiles=3,models = 1)%>%

  get_data(M1_3) %>%

  cbind(d)

This will duplicate the variables used for the LPA, but that’s easily fixed:

M1_3 <- d %>%
  select(ZM_SArt_2_sum, ZEE_M, ZCE_M)%>%
  estimate_profiles(n_profiles=3,models = 1)%>%
  get_data(M1_3)

M1_3 <- cbind(select(d, -ZM_SArt_2_sum, -ZEE_M, -ZCE_M), M1_3)

Josh

--

Date: Monday, April 8, 2019 at 11:52 AM
To: tidyLPA <tid...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: How to return original data frame

Hi am currently working on my first LPA.

To do further analyses I would like to export the data frame with the profile inidcators and a person code which was in the original data frame.

I used the following syntax:

M1_3 <- d %>%
  select(ZM_SArt_2_sum, ZEE_M, ZCE_M)%>%
  estimate_profiles(n_profiles=3,models = 1)%>%
  get_data(M1_3)

However although d has 1661 variables and only three are used for the profiles the M1_3 dataframe has only 9 variables all of them concerning the estimated model but none of the original data besides my three indicator variables.

How can I return a data frame with the model information as profile and probability, and variables of the original data frame?

Thank you so much!

--
